body:
I think its impossible for what you've described to happen. You can use the /db/file endpoint to query the version of the file, which can explain if its being modified in one or more places.

If this was a bug, it should happen to every single file.

I think what can potentially happen is that modification timestamp of the file gets adjusted by some piece of software you have on the side which is not modifying the file content, but the metadata, which is still a valid reason for a conflict.
Also, -verbose -audit options could show something, but I think you are probably syncing something you shouldn't (a running/active database for example) hence why it happens.

I noticed this strange sync-conflicts while editing .odt files and editing images with gimp. So it isn't a active db or so.
I will try to reproduce it with -verbose -audit and see if i can find a useful output. Is there any STTRACE option which shows the detected conflicts ?

No, there isn't. You already know what conflicts were detected by looking at the file names that had the suffix appended. Also, I am guessing you are using inotify for the conflict to happen immediately? It could also be due to some wierd file locking, but you should see errors in the logs (without any extra debug flags) in that case. Also, it potentially could be some sort of indexing software, like picasa, detecting a new file, adding it to a gallery and updating the jpeg/png header about which gallery its in, essentially leaving the viewable image intact, but modifying the content.

As far as i know, i do not use inotify, at least i did not configure for it :-) 
Also it should not be something like picasa as it also happens with .odt file, .c files and many more file types. Its really strange (and pretty dangerious, as i now often have old content in the file and my new content moved to the conflict file) .:-) 
I looked at the log file but can not find any errors regarding the conflicts. There is only one repeating error, that it can not delete a specific directory because it is not empty, and then it pauses the puller for a minute and then continues. 
Maybe the error is somehow related, with changes happening maybe when the puller is paused ? 

For the logs: I am looking for some option to find out why syncthing thinks this is a conflict, when the file is changed locally. The timestamp should be newer then the last one in the index, so it should treat it as a new version, not a conflict. 
Maybe i should dig into the source myself :-)

Attached is a zip file with the syncthing.log and the audit log while such strange conflicts where generated. The affected files where 197.jpg, 198.jpg and 199.jpg. This time the conflict files contained older data...

Not sure if this logs help to debug the issue...

[logs.zip](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/files/63076/logs.zip)

To prevent any issues with deleted and recreated files i just did another test in a new folder (LB1180_2).
Put the images into this folder and waited till they where synced to the other system. Then i modified them locally and monitored the filesystem on both systems. 
This time it uploaded the modified files to the remote system but somehow decided they where conflicts and not updates on the remote system. So it created the sync-conflict files on the remote system and then sync those back to me. 
Affected files: 135.jpg 174.jpg 179.jpg 190.jpg 191.jpg, 192.jpg 193.jpg 194.jpg 195.jpg 196.jpg 
Files in the same folder but somehow synced without conflict: 197.jpg 198.jpg

I hope this logs somehow help to debug this. If you have any suggestions on what i should try, please tell me.
[logs.zip](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/files/63113/logs.zip)

Right. The logs don't contain anything obvious.
Try this build http://build.syncthing.net/job/syncthing-pr/1349/ with STTRACE=conflict

Thank you for your fast response :-) 

I installed this build on the local and the remote system with the STTRACE option. And did the same test again. 
Again the bogus conflict was detected on the remote system on the following files
135.jpg, 174.jpg, 191.jpg, 192.jpg, 193.jpg,194.jpg
the other 5 files where correctly synced.

Attached you will find the log from the remote system. 
Some more information about the remote system: Its a Windows Server2008 and the Data sits on a NAS storage system.
[syncthing.zip](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/files/63181/syncthing.zip)
Also, it seems that the first file we alread have only has 5 blocks, and the new file has 7 blocks, so the content is definitely different and not conflicting with itself.
This sounds like a straight "concurrent modification" kind of conflict to me? Different version counters, different size...

Well, the only suspicion I have is if we advertise version 1, and before we get acknowledged that everyone has version one, and we produce version 2, why does the fact that someone now has version 1 (which is our old version) cause a conflict?

I think conflicts should only happen from two different devices having the same max version, rather than some device having some older version?

Just to clarify i will describe again what i have done to generate this logs:
1. Create files on TAQLGAQ and wait till they are synced (visible in the filesystem) to MC5WCAZ  
2. Modify the files (they got smaller) on TAQLGAQ 
3. After some time they get to MC5WCAZ  but somehow MC5WCAZ determines it is a conflict and not a update (for 6 out of 10) files, so it creates conflict files for those.
4. the conflict files get synced back to me.

I have this problem since version 12.x, and it happens nearly everytime in some different variation (depending on which system detects the bogus conflict). 

If i can do something to debug this problem further, please tell me, as currently synthing is not really useable for me.

Do you have rate limiting set to very low on either side? Or a disproportionate link speed?

As I don't see why the other peer would receive an update that the file was successfully downloaded so much later than it actually was, essentially causing this problem.

Also, if you are using some network based mounting system, perhaps some sort of caching is kicking in.

I can guarantee that it's a problem somehow related to your setup, as a lot of users are using syncthing the same way you are, and are not seeing any of the problems you are describing.

Can you monitor the files on the node where they are not supposed to have been modified? This would guarantee that there's nothing automatically changing either the files or their metadata. Maybe loop over them and get both file attributes and hash them constantly until you see the conflict?
There is a utility stwatchfile which helps you do that, you only need to somehow predict which file it will be.

@AudriusButkevicius TAQLGAQ has a outgoing rate limit of 50kb, MC5WCAZ  has no limit but is pretty slow to update as it is not a local system.

I will try this monitoring thing and report back..
I suggest you try and remove the limit, and see if it exhibits the same behaviour.

I have just done this test again. Syncthing version is now 0.12.9.
- I removed the limit on TAQLGAQ 
- startet stwatchfile on one of the files in the set,on MC5WCAZ once it had the first version of the files.
- modified the files on TAQLGAQ 

Result: 
-after some time MC5WCAZ  recieves the updates, but decides that all files are conflicting and generates conflict files. This time it affected all 12 files of the set.
- stwatchfile detected one modification at the time when syncthing overwrites the file with the new version.

So I guess I am still interested in @calmh's answer to my question.

Alternatively, you could try and provide an isolated environment where this is reproducible with some arbitrary set of files.

I just did some tests with older versions to find out when exactly this problem started.
And i get those bogus conflicts with version 0.12.4 but not version 0.12.3. 
Maybe this helps to find out more ?

I don't see anything related to conflicts.. There is only changes to the scanner, but I don't think they have any effect.

https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/compare/v0.12.3...v0.12.4

What kind of box (OS/version) is MC5WCAZ? 

> after some time MC5WCAZ recieves the updates, but decides that all files are conflicting and generates conflict files. This time it affected all 12 files of the set.

this sounds to me like it's doing something freaky with the filesystem. Antivirus? Something that automatically updates metadata or thumbnails in your JPEG? FAT filesystem with limited mtime precision? A combination?
